name: Brow soap / brow styling soap
lead: Brow soap, or brow styling soap, is a waxy or gel-like soap product brushed through eyebrow hairs to hold them upward and brushed out, producing the "fluffy" or "laminated" brow look popular in recent beauty trends. People use it to make brows look fuller, thicker and more defined without tinting or surgery, and it washes off at the end of the day. It belongs to the same functional category as brow gels, which Wikipedia describes as cosmetics that add texture and hold to brows.[1]

Brows matter to overall appearance because they frame the eyes and carry facial expression; research cited in reference works (Godinho et al., 2018) suggests communication is their primary function, and brow shape is part of a recognisable look, as with Audrey Hepburn's thick brows.[1] A styling product that reshapes the brow therefore changes how the upper face reads.
Little published material exists on soap-based brow products specifically. No clinical studies of brow soap were found.

paras: Eyebrow cosmetics include pencils, shaders, brushes, gels that add texture, and powders or eyeshadows used to fill sparse areas.[1] Brow soap is used in the styling-product role: the product is applied to a spoolie or brush and swept through the hairs to set them in position. The look it supports is a voluminous, brushed-up brow, distinct from the thin plucked brows that were fashionable in the 1920s and 1930s.[1]

Reference works trace brow fashion from hikimayu in 8th-century Japan and the removal of brows by some high-status women in the Elizabethan era to thin, heavily plucked brows in the 1920s and 1930s, exemplified by Joan Crawford, and, in the 21st century, microblading.[1] Other grooming options include tweezing, waxing, threading, tinting with permanent dye, brow transplants and brow lifts.[1] Brow soap sits at the temporary, non-invasive end of these options. The Wikipedia article does not itself cover soap brows or lamination.

card.summary: A styling soap that sets brow hairs upward for a fluffy look; a cosmetic with no published research behind it.
card.aka: brow styling soap, brow lamination soap
card.note: No studies found; effect lasts until the product is washed off.

quick.overview:
Brow soap is a styling product brushed through eyebrow hairs to hold them up and out for a fuller, fluffier look. It is part of the broader family of brow gels and cosmetics.

No clinical studies or detailed reference material on brow soap were found.
quick.mechanism: The product coats the brow hairs and holds them in position until it is removed.
quick.risks: No product-specific safety data were found. As with other periocular cosmetics, skin sensitivity reactions are a general consideration.

chain: Soap product applied to a brush and swept through brow hairs
Fuller, brushed-up brow framing the eyes
angle.text: The product holds brow hairs in an upward, brushed-out position so sparse or flat brows look thicker and more groomed. The effect lasts until the product is washed off.
